title: Stored records with the wrong shape are treated as absent with no log
current: Four decoders parse JSON, check the fields, and return undefined when the shape doesn't match, without logging. The caller then behaves as if no record exists.
location: src/server/data/sourcePostDeletion.ts:38 (parseIntent); src/server/data/subscriberTracking.ts:120 (decode); src/server/data/subscriptionAttempt.ts:80 (acceptance evidence); src/server/data/crosspostData.ts:444 (deletion marker)
evidence: Parse exceptions are logged by the surrounding catch, but valid JSON with missing or wrong fields falls through to return undefined. For a deletion intent, that silently drops a pending deletion or verification. For pending tracking, a join's tracking repair never happens. For acceptance evidence, an expired record and a malformed one look identical.
required: Keep returning undefined, but log a warn (no user data) when a value exists and fails validation, naming the record type and which check failed.
tests: Each decoder logs when given valid JSON with a missing required field.

criticality.why: Malformed state silently cancels pending work such as deletions and tracking repairs.
